Anxiety By Type

Targeted tips and strategies for specific types of anxiety and fears.

😰 Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD)

What It Feels Like

Constant worry about many things. Your mind races between worries, making it hard to concentrate or relax.

What Helps

  • Worry Time: Set a specific 15-minute window to worry. Outside this time, notice the worry and delay it
  • Grounding: Use the 5-4-3-2-1 technique throughout the day
  • Movement: Regular exercise significantly reduces GAD symptoms
  • Limit caffeine: Can amplify anxiety
  • Challenge thoughts: Question your worries - what evidence is there? What's the worst that could happen and could you handle it?

😱 Social Anxiety

What It Feels Like

Fear of social situations, judgment, being watched, or embarrassing yourself. Avoidance of social events.

What Helps

  • Gradual Exposure: Start small - one person vs. group, shorter vs. longer visits
  • Have a Plan: Arrive early, have a conversation starter prepared, know where the exit is
  • Focus Outward: Listen to others instead of monitoring yourself
  • Self-Compassion: Remember - most people are worried about themselves, not judging you
  • Practice: Each social interaction is exposure therapy. You're building confidence
  • Join SafeSpace: Start with online communities where you can practice connection safely

✈️ Specific Phobias

What It Feels Like

Intense fear of specific things: flying, heights, spiders, needles, driving, water, etc. Fear seems irrational but feels very real.

What Helps

  • Exposure Therapy: Gradual, repeated exposure to the feared object/situation (with professional support)
  • Education: Learn facts about your fear - understanding reduces irrationality
  • Desensitization: Start with images, then videos, then real exposure
  • Coping Statements: "This discomfort is temporary" "I've done this before"
  • Professional Help: A therapist can guide you through exposure safely

🚗 Agoraphobia

What It Feels Like

Fear of being in situations where escape feels difficult or help unavailable. Often leads to staying home. Can be debilitating.

What Helps

  • Start Home: Small steps to leave the safety zone with support
  • Have a Buddy: Go places with a trusted person first
  • Grounding Tools: Carry items that help ground you (favorite music, phone with supportive contact)
  • Recovery is Slow: Progress may feel small, but any step outward is success
  • Professional Support: Therapy and sometimes medication can help significantly
  • Connect Online: Start with SafeSpace community from home

💔 Trauma & PTSD

What It Feels Like

Intrusive memories, flashbacks, hypervigilance, nightmares, emotional numbness, avoidance of reminders.

What Helps

  • Professional Trauma Therapy: EMDR, CPT, or Trauma-Focused CBT are evidence-based
  • Safety First: Create physical and emotional safety in your environment
  • Grounding: Essential when experiencing flashbacks or intrusive thoughts
  • Self-Compassion: Your reactions are normal responses to abnormal events
  • Peer Support: Connect with others who understand trauma in SafeSpace
  • Patience: Trauma recovery takes time. Celebrate small victories

😴 Anxiety About Sleep

What It Feels Like

Fear of not sleeping, racing thoughts at bedtime, waking up in panic, fear of the night itself.

What Helps

  • Sleep Hygiene: Consistent schedule, cool dark room, no screens 30min before bed
  • Relaxation: Meditation, progressive muscle relaxation, or guided sleep meditation
  • Acceptance: Trying harder to sleep makes it worse. Accept wakefulness - rest is healing too
  • Get Out of Bed: If anxious for 20min, get up and do a calm activity, return when sleepy
  • Limit Naps: Can interfere with nighttime sleep
  • Breathing Exercises: 4-7-8 breathing is especially good for sleep

💊 Health Anxiety

What It Feels Like

Excessive worry about having a serious illness, constant body checking, frequent doctor visits, fear of symptoms.

What Helps

  • Limit Checking: Resist the urge to check symptoms or research online
  • Resist Reassurance: Getting reassurance provides temporary relief then anxiety returns
  • See Doctor Once: Get a thorough checkup, then trust the results
  • Challenge Thoughts: "What evidence do I have?" "How many times has this worried turned out to be real?"
  • Accept Uncertainty: We can't know 100% we're healthy - learning to live with this uncertainty helps
  • Cognitive Therapy: Very effective for health anxiety

🎓 Performance Anxiety

What It Feels Like

Fear of public speaking, tests, performances, or doing something while being watched. Worry about messing up.

What Helps

  • Practice: The more prepared you are, the less anxious you'll be
  • Normalize Anxiety: Your body is just helping you perform - use that energy
  • Breathing: Practice calming breathing before the performance
  • Reframe: "Excitement" and "anxiety" have the same physical symptoms. Call it excitement!
  • Exposure: Start small (present to 2 people) and gradually increase audience
  • Focus on Content: Remember your audience wants you to succeed

Remember

These categories often overlap, and everyone's experience is unique. A therapist can help identify what you're experiencing and create a personalized plan. You're not alone in any of these - many people are navigating the same fears and finding their way forward.
